fr:mainmatter.html:p: The notion of a displayed algebra does not seem to receive much (or any) recognition in the classical algebra literature (I couldn't find any references to "displayed monoids", "displayed groups", etc.). But displayed structures play a key role in the generalized algebra advocated here, so it's worth examining the displayed analogues of classical algebraic structures. I think the resulting notions are interesting, and deserve further study.

One important class of examples of displayed algebras are actions. The simplest case are the actions of semigroup on a set. Recall that a semigroup is just a set equipped with an associative binary operation:
2026523https://genalg.info/SemiGrp.algSemiGrp.alg/SemiGrp.algSemigroups (\mathfrak {SemiGrp}{\operatorname -}\mathsf {Alg})Definition
A \mathfrak {SemiGrp}-algebra consists of

\mathsf {M} \colon  \mathsf {Set}

\mathsf {m} \colon  \mathsf {M} \to  \mathsf {M} \to  \mathsf {M}

\mathsf {assoc} \colon  \lparen {}x \;y \;z \colon  \mathsf {M}\rparen {}  \to  \mathsf {m}\;x\;\lparen {}\mathsf {m}\;y\;z\rparen {}\;=\;\mathsf {m}\;\lparen {}\mathsf {m}\;x\;y\rparen {}\;z
Now, given a set Z, we define a (left) action of a semigroup (\mathsf {M},\mathsf {m}) on Z as an operation (often written as an infix \bullet ) \_\bullet \_ \colon  \mathsf {M} \times  Z \to  Z  which is compatible with the semigroup operation \mathsf {m}: for all x,y\colon \mathsf {M} and z\colon  Z, x \bullet  (y\bullet  z) = (\mathsf {m}\;x\;y) \bullet  z. There is also the notion of right action, where the semigroup elements "act on the right" (the \bullet  has type Z\times \mathsf {M}\to  Z instead, and the compatibility requirement is adjusted accordingly). This emergent duality is a feature of numerous GATs that include binary operations, most prominently categories.

What's the connection to displayed algebra? Well, it's rather elegant: for each semigroup (\mathsf {M},\mathsf {m}) and set Z: the notion of "action of (\mathsf {M},\mathsf {m}) on Z" is a displayed semigroup over (\mathsf {M},\mathsf {m}), and every such action is a section of this displayed semigroup.

Let's unpack this. A displayed semigroup over a semigroup (\mathsf {M},\mathsf {m}) is a family of sets, indexed by \mathsf {M}, with an associative heterogeneous binary relation over \mathsf {m}. 2026523https://genalg.info/SemiGrp.dalgSemiGrp.dalg/SemiGrp.dalgDisplayed Semigroups (\mathfrak {SemiGrp}{\operatorname -}\mathsf {DAlg})Definition
A displayed \mathfrak {SemiGrp}-algebra (over a \mathfrak {SemiGrp}-algebra (\mathsf {M}, \mathsf {m}, \mathsf {assoc})) consists of
\mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf D} \colon \mathsf {M} \to \mathsf {Set}
\mathsf {m}{}^{\mathsf D} \colon \{x \colon \mathsf {M}\} \lparen {}x{}^{\mathsf D} \colon \mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf D}\;x\rparen {} \{y \colon \mathsf {M}\} \lparen {}y{}^{\mathsf D} \colon \mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf D}\;y\rparen {} \to \mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf D}\;\lparen {}\mathsf {m}\;x\;y\rparen {}
\mathsf {assoc}{}^{\mathsf D} \colon \{x \colon \mathsf {M}\} \lparen {}x{}^{\mathsf D} \colon \mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf D}\;x\rparen {} \{y \colon \mathsf {M}\} \lparen {}y{}^{\mathsf D} \colon \mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf D}\;y\rparen {} \{z \colon \mathsf {M}\} \lparen {}z{}^{\mathsf D} \colon \mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf D}\;z\rparen {} \to \mathsf {m}{}^{\mathsf D}\;x{}^{\mathsf D}\;\lparen {}\mathsf {m}{}^{\mathsf D}\;y{}^{\mathsf D}\;z{}^{\mathsf D}\rparen {}\;=\;\mathsf {m}{}^{\mathsf D}\;\lparen {}\mathsf {m}{}^{\mathsf D}\;x{}^{\mathsf D}\;y{}^{\mathsf D}\rparen {}\;z{}^{\mathsf D} A section of (\mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf D},\mathsf {m}{}^{\mathsf D}) is an assignment: to each x\colon \mathsf {M}, an element of \mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf D}\;x, appropriately compatible with \mathsf {m} and \mathsf {m}{}^{\mathsf D}: 2026523https://genalg.info/SemiGrp.sectSemiGrp.sect/SemiGrp.sectSections of Displayed Semigroups (\mathfrak {SemiGrp}{\operatorname -}\mathsf {Sect})Definition
A section of a displayed \mathfrak {SemiGrp}-algebra (\mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf D}, \mathsf {m}{}^{\mathsf D}, \mathsf {assoc}{}^{\mathsf D}) (over a \mathfrak {SemiGrp}-algebra (\mathsf {M}, \mathsf {m}, \mathsf {assoc})) consists of
\mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf S} \colon \lparen {}x \colon \mathsf {M}\rparen {} \to \mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf D}\;x
\mathsf {m}{}^{\mathsf S} \colon \{x \;y \colon \mathsf {M}\} \to \mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf S}\;\lparen {}\mathsf {m}\;x\;y\rparen {}\;=\;\mathsf {m}{}^{\mathsf D}\;\lparen {}\mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf S}\;x\rparen {}\;\lparen {}\mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf S}\;y\rparen {} We obtain the displayed semigroup of actions on Z by putting \mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf D}\;x to be the set of endofunctions Z\to Z for each x. Jacob Neumann202652https://genalg.info/000D/000D/000D/Displayed semigroups of actionsDefinition
Given a semigroup (\mathsf {M},\mathsf {m}) and a set Z, define the displayed semigroups of actions of (\mathsf {M},\mathsf {m}) on Z by putting \mathsf {M}{}^{\mathsf D}\;x := Z \to Z for all x\colon \mathsf {M}, and then obtain
the displayed semigroup of left actions by putting \mathsf {m}{}^{\mathsf D}\;x{}^{\mathsf D}\;y{}^{\mathsf D} := x{}^{\mathsf D} \circ y{}^{\mathsf D}
the displayed semigroup of right actions by putting \mathsf {m}{}^{\mathsf D}\;x{}^{\mathsf D}\;y{}^{\mathsf D} := y{}^{\mathsf D} \circ x{}^{\mathsf D}. In either case, \mathsf {assoc}{}^{\mathsf D} is a consequence of the associativity of composition.
